findings.title: Materials' 65-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials sits at the 25th percentile on forward earnings but the 90th on trailing, a 65-point split that implies 119 percent growth next year. The market is pricing a near-doubling of earnings, not a cyclical uptick — a bet that current margins are the anomaly, not the base.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' rich trailing multiple looks stale
findings.body: Staples trades at the 93rd percentile on trailing earnings yet only the 47th on forward, a 45-point gap. The 52 percent implied growth is trying to justify a multiple that has already run — the forward lens is effectively discounting the sector's defensive premium.

findings.title: Information Technology's forward cheapness is a growth wager
findings.body: IT's forward multiple sits at the 14th percentile while trailing is at the 60th, a 46-point divergence. The 69 percent implied earnings growth is the market's way of saying today's earnings are depressed — but that's a large assumption for a sector whose forward percentile has dropped nine points in a month.
